status_summary: A presidential memorandum of 2025-01-20 directed Commerce and USTR to review trade deficits, unfair foreign trade practices and existing trade agreements; it applies to all major partners and does not name the EU or UK. Executive Order 14309 (signed 2025-06-16) implemented the US-UK Economic Prosperity Deal's auto, aerospace and metals terms, and a US-EU joint statement of 2025-08-21, which calls itself a first step, had its tariff elements implemented by a Federal Register notice of 2025-09-25. After the Supreme Court held on 2026-02-20 that the emergency-powers statute does not authorize tariffs, a presidential memorandum of 2026-07-23 set Section 301 duties from 2026-07-24 at a combined 10 percent for most EU goods and a flat 10 percent for the UK, EU Regulation 2026/1455 has applied EU duty concessions on US goods since 2026-07-01, and a Commerce notice of 2026-08-04 cut the tariff on patented UK pharmaceuticals to zero. The approach is a government-wide, tariff-driven review followed by deals, not an EU-specific review, and 25 states have challenged the Section 301 duties in court.

timeline.event: The America First Trade Policy memorandum directed Commerce and USTR to report by 2025-04-01 on the causes of persistent trade deficits, on unfair trade practices by other countries, and on revisions to existing trade agreements needed for reciprocal concessions; it does not name the EU or UK.
The US and UK announced the general terms of the Economic Prosperity Deal, per USTR's listing.

Executive Order 14309 (signed 2025-06-16, published 2025-06-23 at 90 FR 26419) implements the general terms of the US-UK Economic Prosperity Deal: a 100,000-vehicle annual quota of UK-made cars at a 10 percent combined rate, an end to certain tariffs on UK civil aircraft products, and a direction to Commerce to set tariff-rate quotas for UK steel and aluminum at a later time.

The US and EU issue a joint statement on a framework for an agreement on reciprocal, fair and balanced trade: a combined 15 percent ceiling on most EU goods, EU tariff elimination on US industrial goods, mutual acceptance of auto standards, energy and investment pledges and digital trade commitments; it calls itself a first step, uses intent language for many items and does not say it is legally binding.

A Commerce and USTR Federal Register notice (90 FR 46136, effective 2025-09-25) amends the tariff schedule to implement tariff-related elements of the US-EU framework: listed EU products and aircraft parts are exempted from reciprocal tariffs, and automobile tariffs under Proclamation 10908 are removed where the most-favored-nation rate is 15 percent or higher and otherwise reduced so the combined rate is 15 percent, with the automobile changes applying to goods entered from 2025-08-01 and the aircraft changes from 2025-09-01; the notice relies on Executive Order 14346.
The Supreme Court held 6-3 in Learning Resources v. Trump that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act does not authorize tariffs.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States

timeline.event: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, adopted 2026-06-25, applies from 2026-07-01 until 2029-12-31: it sets zero EU duties on listed US-origin goods, opens tariff quotas for certain US agricultural and seafood products, and allows the Commission to suspend these concessions if the US does not implement the 2025-08-21 joint statement, with a recital referring to a 15 percent all-inclusive US tariff ceiling.

A presidential memorandum to the Trade Representative in the Section 301 forced-labor investigations (published 2026-07-28 at 91 FR 47717) sets the EU Section 301 duty so that it and the most-favored-nation rate combine to 10 percent, with no added duty where that rate is 10 percent or more, and sets a flat 10 percent for the UK.

Additional duties under Section 301 apply from 2026-07-24 per the USTR Federal Register notice of 2026-07-28 (91 FR 47318), which concludes forced-labor investigations of 60 economies: the EU rate is set so the most-favored-nation duty plus the Section 301 duty equals 10 percent, and the UK faces a flat 10 percent.

A Commerce Bureau of Industry and Security notice (91 FR 49406) lowers the US tariff on patented pharmaceuticals and pharmaceutical ingredients from the UK from 10 percent to 0 percent under Proclamation 11020, effective for goods entered from 2026-07-31, citing the US-UK pharmaceutical pricing arrangement.

United States (No. 26-01606), signed by Chief Judge Barnett and Judge Kelly and read in a RECAP copy on courtlistener.com on 2026-10-26, declares Proclamation 11012 invalid as contrary to law; per the research pass it permanently enjoins the surcharge as to the State of Washington and the importer plaintiffs, with refunds with interest. The accompanying opinion and any appeal were not read. The proclamation's issuance on 2026-02-20, effective date of 2026-02-24 and expiry on 2026-07-24, and continued collection from non-plaintiff importers after the judgment, rest on a Holland & Knight summary of 2026-05-08. The stacking concern and the UK digital services tax proposal rest on law-firm trackers, not on primary documents. The April 2025 reports produced under the trade memorandum were not read, so how far they addressed EU arrangements specifically is unknown. The date of the UK White House fact sheet is approximate. The EU regulation was read in full (EUR-Lex HTML) in review; its recitals refer to a temporary US import surcharge under Section 122 proclaimed on 2026-02-20, which is consistent with the law-firm reports. Most EU products facing a 15 percent US rate from July 2026 rests on a law-firm tracker. Inference: match was changed to partial because the Mandate asks for a fairness and reciprocity review and closer UK trade, which the memorandum's review and the resulting deals address in substance, though by tariff leverage and not by an EU-specific review. The trade-promotion-authority and wider agreements framework is covered in c26-05. A coalition of 25 states (New York joining 24 others, per the New York Governor's release of 2026-08-03) filed suit at the Court of International Trade on 2026-08-03 against the Section 301 forced-labor tariffs that now set the EU and UK rates, asking the court to declare them illegal and seeking refunds; the Oregon Department of Justice federal litigation tracker records the filing that day and a court order of 2026-08-19 staying the states' case while the court adjudicates a sample case. The stay order, the complaint and the docket were not read, no injunction or merits ruling was found, and the suit is not reflected in court_status. The 2026-08-04 UK pharmaceutical notice was issued under Proclamation 11020 of 2026-04-02 and a US-UK pharmaceutical pricing arrangement announced the same day; the proclamation and the arrangement were not read.
